title: Roadmap Confidence Index and Exec Ask Playbook
creator: Marissa Chen
description:
Purpose: Provide a concise, repeatable exec readout artifact that quantifies roadmap confidence, surfaces unresolved risks, and packages decision-level asks so leadership can commit funding/heads or reprioritize. This ticket produces a playbook and the first public Roadmap Confidence Index (RCI) for QBR review.

What the RCI is: a single composite score (0-100) summarizing initiative readiness across four pillars: scope stability (30%), engineering velocity (30%), cross-functional dependencies (20%), and measurable outcomes (20%). Each pillar has defined signals and a normalization rubric. The RCI is intended to complement (not replace) qualitative narratives and risk registers.

Deliverables: 1) RCI scoring sheet (CSV + view in dashboard), 2) Exec readout one-pager + 2-slide ask packet per initiative, 3) Consolidated risk heatmap with mitigations, 4) Action tracker with owners and SLAs for decision items.

Decision asks we will surface to execs: tiered investment asks (no-regret vs. conditional), runway adjustments for low-RCI initiatives, and explicit go/no-go gates for any initiative with RCI < 45. Each ask includes the blocker, cost (ops + eng), and recommended timeline.

Scope exclusions: does not re-score active incidents or post-mortem outcomes; those remain in SRE/incident channels. The playbook excludes marketing launch assets (handled by GTM) but flags gating dependencies (e.g., data contracts, compliance signoffs).

Success criteria for this ticket: RCI scoring completed for top 12 initiatives, exec readout materials accepted by PLs and VP of Product, three prioritized decision asks agreed at the QBR, and action tracker with owners for all red/amber items.

How to compute RCI (high level):
- Scope stability: percent of planned scope with clear acceptance criteria and no outstanding unresolved technical questions (0-30).
- Engineering velocity: forecast burn vs. baseline velocity adjusted for known blockers and holidays (0-30).
- Dependencies: count of external dependencies weighted by criticality and time-to-resolution (0-20).
- Outcomes confidence: presence of measurable success metrics and validated experiments or prototypes (0-20).

Readout agenda (20 minutes per initiative slot):
1) One-sentence initiative summary (30s)
2) RCI score & pillar breakdown (90s)
3) Top 3 risks and proposed mitigations (180s)
4) Decision ask(s) with clear options and recommended action (120s)
5) Q&A and capture of follow-ups (60s)

Artifacts and links: Confluence RCI rubric (drive.redwood.com/rcirubric), Google Sheet scoring workbook (drive.redwood.com/rcisheet), Dashboard (grafana.redwood.com/d/roadmap/rc-dashboard), Draft exec packet (docs.redwood.com/roadmap-readout-2025-q1), PRs for supporting work (github.com/redwood-inference/pipeline/pull/482), cost model snapshot (s3.redwood.com/inference-econ/2025-q1.csv).

Review expectations: Ask ENG/Design/Privacy to verify pillar inputs by 2025-03-14. PM owners to upload evidence links for each pillar in the scoring sheet by 2025-03-16. Finalized one-pager to be circulated to the exec committee by 2025-03-18.

Risks & mitigations (summary):
- High: Two initiatives depend on external infra team delivery (ETA mismatch). Mitigation: escalate for dedicated pipe, offer pair engineering support, or break initiative into a no-regret MVP.
- Medium: Ambiguous success metrics on three initiatives. Mitigation: rapid metric definition workshop with Research and Analytics.
- Low: Console dashboard refresh collides with release window. Mitigation: carve out a read-only staging dashboard for the QBR.

Stakeholder ask list: VP Product (approve asks), Head of Eng (commit resource lanes), Head of Infra (dependency resolution), Finance (confirm runway for tiered asks), Legal/Compliance (flag gating items requiring signoff).

Communication plan: Post-acceptance, publish an exec readout packet to Confluence and send a summary email with action tracker links. Follow-up cadence: weekly 15-min sync on action items until closed.
